An opportunity has arisen for an Assistant Accountant to join the team, supporting the delivery of bookkeeping, payroll and accounts preparation services to a varied client base.

- Previous experience working within an accountancy practice is essential.

- Good attention to detail and a commitment to producing accurate work.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage workloads effectively.
- Good written and verbal communication skills.
- A proactive approach with a willingness to learn and develop new skills.
- Competent IT skills, with experience using accounting software being advantageous.

- Working Hours:5 hours per week.

- Office Environment: A collaborative and supportive workplace, with opportunities to learn directly from experienced colleagues.

- Salary: Approximately £25,000, depending on experience.
- Annual Leave: 25 days' annual leave, plus bank holidays.
- Study Support: Financial support of up to £500 per exam or module towards eligible AAT, ACCA or CTA studies, reimbursed following successful completion of probation.

- Hybrid Working: The opportunity to work from home following successful completion of probation.
- Career Progression: Clear opportunities to progress into more senior accounting positions as technical knowledge and experience develop.
- Training & Development: Practical, on-the-job training and support from experienced members of the team.

title: Insurance Lead Generator
description:
Fully Remote Available Up to £45,000 Basic + Generous Bonus Leeds-Based Independent Broker

A lead generation role where quality matters more than call statistics.

If you're good at generating new business opportunities but frustrated by unrealistic call targets, poor-quality data or pressure to book appointments for the sake of it, this could be worth a conversation.

I'm recruiting for a growing independent commercial insurance broker that's looking for an experienced Contact Manager to help develop its commercial business.

This isn't a typical high-volume telesales position.

They're not expecting you to make 150-200 calls a day or fill an Account Executive's diary with meetings that have little chance of going anywhere.

They'd much rather you research a business properly, understand who you're speaking to and have a worthwhile conversation that could eventually lead to a new client.

They appreciate that good opportunities take time to develop, particularly in commercial insurance, where renewal dates and established relationships play such an important part.

And importantly, you'll be rewarded for the results you deliver.

What would you be doing?

You'll be working closely with experienced Commercial Account Executives, identifying businesses that could benefit from reviewing their insurance arrangements.

The good news is that you won't be starting from scratch.

The company already has an established, cleansed database of business contacts and insurance renewal dates, giving you a strong starting point.

Alongside developing these existing prospects, you'll also research and identify new businesses to approach, with a particular interest in growing their presence within the construction sector.

Your role will involve identifying the right decision-makers, understanding their business and insurance renewal dates, developing relationships and arranging qualified appointments.

And when it comes to what constitutes a good appointment, they're sensible.

They're not expecting you to complete a full insurance review before arranging a meeting. At a minimum, they're looking for a genuine prospect who's open to discussing their arrangements at renewal, with some understanding of what might encourage them to consider another broker.

The more information you can obtain, the better, but they recognise that every opportunity is different.

Ultimately, they want someone who understands the difference between a name in a diary and a genuine commercial opportunity.

Who are they looking for?

Ideally, you'll already have experience generating new business opportunities within commercial insurance.

You'll understand how the renewal cycle works, be comfortable talking to business owners and decision-makers, and have a proven track record of identifying opportunities that result in new business.

For someone who can demonstrate this experience and success, there's a basic salary of up to circa £45,000 available.

However, insurance experience isn't essential.

They're also interested in speaking with successful B2 B lead generation professionals who have a consultative approach, strong research skills and the ability to build relationships with senior decision-makers.

For someone coming from outside insurance, the salary is likely to be around £35,000, although there's flexibility for an exceptional candidate.

What matters most is that you're commercially aware, naturally curious, confident on the telephone and genuinely enjoy the challenge of opening doors.

A role you can make your own

The company has already enjoyed considerable success with its lead generation function and recognises just how important the right person can be to its growth.

This is a key appointment, rather than simply another person being brought in to make calls.

They're equally happy to recruit someone who wants to establish themselves as a successful, well-rewarded Contact Manager for the long term, or someone who has ambitions to develop into a client-facing Commercial Account Executive role.

There's no expectation that you have to move into an Account Executive position to progress or be valued.

If you're excellent at generating opportunities and want to continue doing that, they'll appreciate what you bring.

Equally, if your longer-term ambitions involve managing clients and developing your own portfolio, it's a business where that conversation can be had.

What's on offer?
- Up to £45,000 basic salary for someone with a successful track record in commercial insurance lead generation.
- Generous bonus scheme, rewarding you for qualified appointments and paying a percentage of income generated from successful new business.
- Fully remote working available, with the option to spend time in the office on the outskirts of Leeds if you're local. Free parking is available.
- An existing, cleansed database of business contacts and insurance renewal dates.
- The opportunity to develop new prospect relationships, particularly within construction.
- Sensible, commercially focused expectations rather than excessive call-volume targets.
- A growing independent broker that recognises and rewards the contribution of its people.
- The opportunity to build a long-term career in lead generation or potentially develop towards an Account Executive position, depending on your ambitions.

Interested?

If you're already successful in commercial insurance lead generation but feel you could achieve more with the right backing, realistic expectations and a rewarding bonus structure, I'd be particularly interested in speaking with you.

Equally, if you've developed a strong track record in B2 B lead generation and fancy applying those skills within commercial insurance, this could be an excellent opportunity.

You don't need to be actively looking for something new.

Get in touch for a confidential conversation, and I'll happily explain more about the business, the people involved and what they're looking to achieve.

title: Receptionist
description: We are a busy GP Surgery and due to an ever increasing list size and the relocation of one our receptionists we are looking to recruit a highly motivated, professional individual with excellent Customer Service Skills to join our friendly team. We are looking for full time or part time . If part time we are looking for afternoon cover till 6/6:30p.m. The role includes dealing with our patients over the telephone and face to face, undertaking administrative tasks, prescriptions and many other tasks that support our patients and the clinicians. Experience would be beneficial, however not essential. We are looking for a professional, highly motivated individual with excellent customer service and communication skills. Someone who is willing to work as part of a team and can also work on their own initiative. Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. Provide general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone Job responsibilities: Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the practice Deal with all general enquiries, explain procedures and make new and follow-up appointments. Using your own judgment and communication skills ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner. Explain practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover and ensure procedures are completed. Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. Enter requests for home visits into the visit book, ensuring careful recording of all relevant details and where necessary refer to duty doctor. Action repeat prescription requests and ensure that they are ready for collection by the patient within 48 hours, either on the computer or manually. Prepare lists and notes for all surgeries and clinics held, ensuring completion of all associated paperwork. Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non General Medical Services) services, accept payment and issue receipts for same. Enter patient information on to the computer as required. Patient notes and correspondence: Make and serve refreshments, ensure the kitchen is kept clean and tidy and air and tidy the waiting room in turn with other staff. Ensure that all new patients are registered onto the computer system promptly and accurately Undertake any other additional duties appropriate to the post as requested by the Partners or the practice manager. Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately In the performance of the duties outlined in this job description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data Health & safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice health & safety policy, the practice health & safety manual, and the practice infection control policy and published procedures. This will include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Actively reporting of health and safety hazards and infection hazards immediately when recognised Keeping own work areas and general / patient areas generally clean, assisting in the maintenance of general standards of cleanliness consistent with the scope of the job holders role Undertaking periodic infection control training (minimum annually) Reporting potential risks identified Equality and diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognizes the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/professional development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication: The post-holder should recognize the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognize peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the implementation of services: The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate

title: Care Navigator/ Medical Receptionist
description: South Queen Street Medical Centre are looking to appoint a care navigator/ receptionist to join our busy GP practice who will be the first point of contact for patients, contractors, and visitors as well as carrying out general office management tasks. Working pattern 5 hours per day, 5 days a week, alternate weekly am & pm shifts, 8am-630pm. Flexibility and overtime will be required for this role. You will be responsible for the general reception duties within the Practice and work with our established processes, policies, and procedures to provide a comprehensive high-quality service and deal efficiently and courteously with patient enquiries. You will receive, assist, and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. You will provide general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone. You will have excellent communication skills, a compassionate and friendly nature who can operate in a busy environment with a range of people and professions, as you will be working with our clinical and administration teams. This role is ideal for someone who is highly organised and an effective communicator who can provide a professional and warm welcome to our patients, ensuring every contact is of the highest quality. IT skills are essential, as you will be regularly creating searches, data input and monitoring our achievements and progress against national, local, and internal targets. You will also process prescription requests and provide a full administrative service. GCSE grade C or above in English and Maths is essential for this role. Key Duties and Responsibilities Patient Reception and Customer Service Act as the first point of contact for patients, visitors and healthcare professionals, both face-to-face and over the telephone. Welcome patients in a friendly, respectful and professional manner. Respond to general enquiries and provide accurate information about practice services, opening hours and appointment procedures. Deal sensitively with patients who may be anxious, distressed, frustrated or experiencing difficult personal circumstances. Maintain a clean, organised and welcoming reception and waiting area. Manage challenging situations professionally and escalate complaints or concerns to the appropriate member of the practice team. Care Navigation and Appointment Management Handle patient requests for appointments, advice and access to healthcare services by telephone and in person. Use approved care navigation protocols to direct patients to the most appropriate clinician or service, including GPs, practice nurses, clinical pharmacists, physiotherapists and other available services where appropriate. Gather relevant non-clinical information to help determine the appropriate appointment pathway, without attempting to diagnose medical conditions. Book, amend and cancel appointments using the practices clinical computer system. Identify potentially urgent concerns in accordance with practice procedures and promptly escalate them to a clinician. Provide information about alternative services, such as NHS 111, where appropriate and in accordance with practice guidance. Maintain accurate records of patient contacts and appointment requests. Telephone and Administrative Duties Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and manage a busy call queue efficiently. Handle patient messages and ensure they are passed to the appropriate member of the clinical or administrative team. Process repeat prescription requests in accordance with practice policies and direct medication queries to the appropriate professional. Register new patients and update demographic details, contact information and other relevant records. Manage incoming and outgoing post, emails and electronic communications. Assist with administrative tasks, including recalling patients for appointments, supporting clinical audits and maintaining accurate practice records. Monitor outstanding administrative tasks and follow up requests within agreed timescales. Clinical Systems and Data Management Use the practices electronic clinical system, SystmOne, to access and update patient information. Ensure patient details, appointment information and messages are recorded accurately and promptly. Handle sensitive patient information securely and maintain strict confidentiality at all times. Comply with UK GDPR, data protection legislation, information governance requirements and practice policies. Follow procedures for accessing, storing and sharing patient information appropriately. Teamwork and Practice Support Work collaboratively with GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants, pharmacists, care coordinators and administrative colleagues. Attend staff meetings and training sessions as required. Support colleagues during busy periods and assist with the day-to-day organisation of reception services. Follow practice policies relating to health and safety, infection prevention, safeguarding and equality and diversity. Report incidents, risks and concerns to the appropriate manager. Undertake other reasonable duties appropriate to the role to support the effective operation of the practice. Training and Development The successful candidate will receive induction and training appropriate to the role, including practice procedures, clinical systems, information governance, confidentiality, safeguarding, health and safety and care navigation. Ongoing training and development will be encouraged to support the delivery of a safe, efficient and high-quality patient service. Personal Qualities We are looking for someone who is approachable, empathetic, dependable and proactive. The successful candidate must demonstrate patience, discretion and professionalism when dealing with sensitive situations and be committed to treating every patient with dignity, respect and fairness. Working Conditions The postholder will work within a busy GP practice and may be required to work flexibly according to the needs of the service. Working hours, salary, annual leave and other employment terms will be confirmed during recruitment.
